maria: hey team — deployed quantized reranker v2 to canary (ptq per-channel). Offline NDCG looks good (+0.8%) but prod CTR on the canary slice is down ~3%. dashboard: https://rbwd/infer/bench/xcv-21. anyone seen this before?

 tom: wow that gap is concerning. did we change candidate generation or only the reranker weights?

 maria: only reranker. same candidate pool, same indexing. quant step: `./quantize --model rerank-v2 --mode perchannel --bits 8`

 li: small score perturbations can reorder topk even if ndcg rises overall. can you share score diffs for a few queries?

 maria: example diff (orig scores -> quantized scores):
```
q1: candA 0.812 -> 0.809  (rank1 -> rank2)
q1: candB 0.808 -> 0.811  (rank2 -> rank1)
q7: candX 0.543 -> 0.542  (no change)
q7: candY 0.539 -> 0.541  (rank3 -> rank2)
```

 anya: that pattern smells like head queries losing exact score ordering. ndcg aggregates can hide head-tail splits. do a stratified slice by query freq.

 tom: run: `evaluate --slice head_queries,tail_queries --metrics ndcg,mrr,top1_precision --topk 5 --baseline rerank-fp`

 julian: if top1 for frequent queries flips, CTR would drop even if long-tail gains boost average ndcg.

 maria: ran quick slice run: head_queries NDCG -1.2% (top1 MRR -2.7%), tail_queries NDCG +2.1%. canaries show negative impact on high-traffic queries. rolling back canary now.

 ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback initiated for canary group xcv-21 at 1745553378. reason: abnormal downstream metric delta (CTR -3%).

 li: hypothesis: quant reduced score granularity near decision boundary and our tie-breaker falls back to doc id lexical order (which correlates poorly with clicks). tie-handling + quant noise = worse top1.

 anya: agreed. options: temperature scaling on scores before sorting, tiny additive jitter to break pathological ties deterministically, or preserve higher-precision for top-k rescoring. also run pairwise metrics (swap-rate, top1 parity) not just ndcg.

 tom: did a micro-experiment: adding gaussian(0,1e-4) noise to FP scores reduced swap-rate vs quantized baseline. obviously hacky but useful to probe mechanism.

 maria: action items: 1) run stratified eval (head/tail) with ndcg,mrr,top1_precision,swap_rate; 2) compare per-tensor vs per-channel PTQ and a small QAT run with pairwise ordering loss (lambda=1e-4); 3) sample 200 head queries for human-label check. i'll spawn benchmark job and log candidate ordering hashes to prod traces.

 anya: :thumbsup: please include raw score diffs and per-candidate click prop in the job so we can correlate reorders with historical CTR.

 julian: also add a prod log flag to persist candidate ordering (ids + ranks) for a small % traffic to help repro.

 maria: thanks — rolling back fully now and will post results in ~24h. /cc @eng-sre
